title: Low-fidelity Venezuelan equine encephalitis virus polymerase mutants to improve live-attenuated vaccine safety and efficacy.
ehr_evidence: The study used in vitro cell cultures (Vero, HEK-293, BHK, C7/10, U4.4) and in vivo murine models (6-day-old and adult CD-1 mice) with Illumina and Sanger sequencing; no electronic/computerised individual-level health records were used.
summary: An experimental in vitro and in vivo study testing low-fidelity RNA-dependent RNA-polymerase (RdRp) mutants of the live-attenuated VEEV vaccine strain TC-83 in cell culture and CD-1 mice to assess attenuation, immunogenicity, and vaccine phenotypic stability.
key_findings: The TC-83 3x mutant produced significantly higher genetic diversity than the parent TC-83, independent of cell type (Illumina sequencing).
TC-83 3x and 4x mutants produced significantly higher mean neutralizing antibody titers compared with TC-83 (repeated measures ANOVA, p = 0.0049 and 0.0012, respectively).
All vaccinated animals showed complete protection from weight loss and death after challenge with VEEV subtype IC strain 3908, whereas sham-vaccinated animals all succumbed by Day 9 post-challenge.
TC-83 3x was significantly more virulent than the parent virus after intracranial injection (p ≤ 0.05, Kaplan-Meier test), with mean time to death of 3.91 days versus 5.36-5.54 days.
TC-83 3x and 4x exhibited significantly reduced mortality when injected subcutaneously compared with parent TC-83 (Kaplan-Meier test, p ≤ 0.05).
TC-83, TC-83 3x and TC-83 4x all gained virulence by passage 5 versus unpassaged counterparts (Kaplan-Meier test, p ≤ 0.0001), but did not exceed parent virulence.
E37G was significantly more sensitive to 5FU than parent TC-83 (p < 0.01 for 50 µg/ml, p < 0.0001 for 100-300 µg/ml).
captured_features: Virus titers (log10 PFU/ml) by plaque assay
Replication kinetics in Vero and HEK-293 cells
study_design: Experimental in vitro and in vivo study (cell culture and murine vaccine/challenge model)
population: 6-day-old and adult (7-week) CD-1 mice and mammalian/insect cell lines (Vero, HEK-293, BHK, C7/10, U4.4)
exposure_domain: Viral RdRp fidelity (low-fidelity) mutations in the TC-83 vaccine strain
limitations: Findings are limited to cell culture and mouse models and do not establish efficacy or safety in humans.
Phenotypic instability driven by minority variants generated during electroporation produced inconsistent attenuation across replicates.
The 4x mutant showed no diversity change after one passage yet behaved as low-fidelity in vivo, indicating single-passage fidelity assessment is insufficient.
data_availability_statement: Data are not publically available, but will be provided upon request.
